chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Najran from Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'In game that is found with an arrow in it, and it is dead, and it is not known who killed it, he said: Do not eat it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating game found dead with an arrow in it when the hunter is unknown?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), quoting Imam Ali (AS), establishes the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) in cases of doubt (*shubha*) regarding the source of death for hunted game. In Shia jurisprudence, the absence of certainty that the animal was slaughtered in the name of Allah or that the hunter's wound caused immediate death renders the meat *makruh* or *haram* to consume, emphasizing caution in matters of food purity. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on verifying the chain of slaughter when the primary condition (the hunter's intent and action) is obscured by uncertainty.
